claims.text: The FeNiCrCoCu coating and Cu matrix are initially single-crystalline, FCC, and have a low intrinsic defect density.
The FeNiCrCoCu/Cu system can be treated as paramagnetic at 900–1200 K because of its high thermal energy.
Above 900 K, longitudinal spin fluctuations become active in the FeNiCrCoCu/Cu system.
Longitudinal spin fluctuations slightly lower FCC-HCP interfacial energy.
The LSF-induced reduction in interfacial energy lowers the barrier for rapid FCC-to-HCP transformation above 900 K.
Thermal activation above 900 K promotes dislocation annihilation and dislocation starvation.
Dislocations provide a primary hardening mechanism, so dislocation starvation removes an important source of strength.
HCP formation combined with loss of dislocation barriers causes a sharp hardness decrease.
HCP formation causes a friction spike through increased mechanical interlocking and phase-boundary sliding.
Lattice-parameter-related friction in an HCP-containing HEA can hinder partial-dislocation motion.
At 900 K and 1200 K, the coefficient of friction increases non-monotonically and hardness decreases sharply relative to 600 K.
At 900 K and 1200 K, HCP atom count increases and total dislocation line length decreases in the indentation zone relative to 600 K.
At 600 K, dislocation density is higher or stable and elastic modulus is increased.
No rapid lattice disorder or HCP phase is present at 600 K.
The proposed mechanism is specific to FCC-based FeNiCrCoCu HEAs under high strain rates.
The mechanism may not apply to BCC HEAs because screw-dislocation mobility dominates their response.
Stable oxide films can lower friction at elevated temperature by smoothing the contact and reducing mechanical interlocking.
Poor oxidation resistance above 600 °C could contribute to the observed high-temperature response.
The exact HCP-nucleation threshold has not been established specifically for FeNiCrCoCu.
Comparing HCP atom counts, dislocation line lengths, friction, and hardness among seeded, dislocation-free, and baseline simulations is proposed as a falsification test.

contradictions.description: The design states that there are two distinct protocols but then enumerates three protocols.

The mechanism treats dislocation annihilation/starvation as a distinct mechanical contribution to softening, whereas the experiment describes an artificially dislocation-free system as isolating thermal softening. This conflates mechanical annealing/dislocation starvation with disorder-driven thermal softening.
